note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — ANNUAL + COARSE HEAD
tiles.details: Trace an attached flowering culm to a fibrous annual base (FNA commonly 15–45(–65) cm). Panicle may be condensed OR open, so neither density nor odor alone establishes stinkgrass. Check mature spikelets and glands. Existing overview photographs do not prove roots or microscopic glands.
tiles.short: Annual tuft with chunky, many-flowered spikelets; smell is only supporting.
tiles.status: FIELD CUE — ROOTED SAME-PLANT PHOTO NEEDED

tiles.heading: 02 · OPEN THE TRUE LIGULE
tiles.details: At the inner blade–sheath junction, distinguish the short true ciliate ligule from the much longer hairs at the outer sheath mouth (to ~5 mm in FNA). Gallery index 3 is an OUTER collar context photograph, index 4 is the blade–sheath junction montage, and index 5 is Stefan.lefnaer's source-identified TRUE inner ligule hair-fringe macro with a printed 3-mm scale. Index 6 is a DIFFERENT species (red lovegrass) and must never illustrate this ligule. The image does not independently validate a 0.4–0.8-mm measurement or a Texas locality.
tiles.short: True ligule is a ~0.4–0.8 mm FRINGE OF HAIRS.
tiles.status: REAL SOURCE-LABELLED LIGULE PHOTO — PRECISE LENGTH NOT PIXEL-VERIFIED

tiles.heading: 03 · PANICLE BRANCHES AND GLAND PITS
tiles.details: FNA describes panicles mostly 5–16(–20) cm long, with stiff primary branches and short pedicels ~0.2–3 mm. Inspect several nodes, pedicels and lemma keels at 10–20× for small crateriform gland pits. Glands vary and may be invisible on a normal field photo; do not draw a gland arrow until actual pits are resolved.
tiles.short: Stout branches ~0.4–5 cm; craterlike glands often on nodes, pedicels or lemma keels.

tiles.heading: 04 · MEASURE ONE MATURE SPIKELET
tiles.details: Isolate one mature spikelet and count overlapping florets in TWO ranks, rather than mistaking an entire flowering branch for one spikelet. FNA's 6–20 mm range is narrower than some global treatments; use the cited treatment and a real millimeter ruler. Existing Harry Rose spikelet photo teaches gross structure, not independently calibrated floret count.
tiles.short: Flattened spikelets mostly 6–20 × 2–4 mm, commonly 10–40 florets.

tiles.heading: 05 · SEPARATE GLUMES, LEMMA AND PALEA
tiles.details: At 20–40× remove the two short basal glumes and expose a mature fertile floret. FNA describes three-veined lemmas with often 1–3 crateriform glands on the keel; palea ~1.2–2.1 mm, its two keels rough and sometimes ciliate. No long lemma awn. Published anatomical ranges are NOT measurements of gallery pixels. No current panel shows separated, calibrated glumes, lemma and palea: this teaching tile intentionally has NO image reference until a real dissection is added.
tiles.short: Lower glume ~1.2–2 mm (usually 1 vein); upper ~1.2–2.6 mm (often 3); lemma ~2–2.8 mm, 3-veined, AWNLESS.

tiles.heading: 06 · CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES + RELEASE GATE
tiles.details: E. secundiflora is perennial, often with clustered reddish spikelets but red color overlaps; E. spectabilis has a loose spreading cloud; E. intermedia has a finer open panicle; other introduced annual Eragrostis require ripe floret examination. NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: one Texas-vouchered rooted annual with mature head, opened true ligule, side-lit gland-pit macro, and millimeter-scale glume/lemma dissection. NEEDS_SITE_QA: inspect eight existing image records, distinguish local JPEGs from remote records, verify each CC/CC0 permission and photographer credit, image labels, arrow endpoints and actual mobile gallery rendering. Remain FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS.
tiles.short: Separate native perennial red lovegrass from introduced annual stinkgrass using base + glandular spikelet.

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: First check the stout, relatively dense, many-flowered spikelets and ANNUAL habit. Under 10–20× look for distinctive craterlike/wartlike GLANDS on inflorescence branches, pedicels, glume or lemma keels (variable; not all photos show them). Fresh plants may smell strong when crushed, but odor is a secondary clue.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: START with the source-verified 10-mm montage of actual leaf sheaths and blades: identify the OUTSIDE blade–sheath junction in multiple angles.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: At the inner blade–sheath junction, distinguish the short true ciliate ligule from the much longer hairs at the outer sheath mouth (to ~5 mm in FNA). Gallery index 3 is an OUTER collar context photograph, index 4 is the blade–sheath junction montage, and index 5 is Stefan.lefnaer's source-identified TRUE inner ligule hair-fringe macro with a printed 3-mm scale. Index 6 is a DIFFERENT species (red lovegrass) and must never illustrate this ligule. The image does not independently validate a 0.4–0.8-mm measurement or a Texas locality.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: FNA describes panicles mostly 5–16(–20) cm long, with stiff primary branches and short pedicels ~0.2–3 mm. Inspect several nodes, pedicels and lemma keels at 10–20× for small crateriform gland pits. Glands vary and may be invisible on a normal field photo; do not draw a gland arrow until actual pits are resolved.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: E. secundiflora can also have large dense spikelets but is a perennial and has different panicle architecture; glands on branchlets/lemma keel are especially worth checking in cilianensis. E. intermedia / E. spectabilis usually look more open with scattered smaller spikelets. Other introduced annual lovegrasses may require dissection; distinguish E. pectinacea using mature spikelet structure and glands, not odor only.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

panels.label: Stinkgrass — individual spikelets source photograph
panels.caption: Actual Harry Rose photograph of several pale, later-season flattened spikelets on slender branches. The upper-left arrow identifies one complete spikelet; the second points to visibly overlapping floret units in another spikelet. No ruler is present. Individual glumes versus lemmas, nerve counts, craterlike gland pits, and exact dimensions cannot be verified from these pixels.

panels.label: Stinkgrass — true collar source photograph
panels.caption: Harry Rose's original source photograph visibly shows a blade–sheath junction and long pale hairs projecting from the collar region. These outer hairs must NOT be labelled the true ligule: the inner hair-fringe boundary and its length are not resolved. Australian source-labelled E. cilianensis, CC BY 2.0; existing archived JPEG not independently byte-retrievable this run. No anatomical arrows added.
